movesets.name: Stealth Rock
movesets.description:
Garganacl is an exceptional Stealth Rock setter and wall thanks to its great bulk, amazing ability in Purifying Salt, and access to Salt Cure. As a setter, Garganacl is very good at outlasting and pressuring common removal options like non-Leftovers Great Tusk, Corviknight, and Iron Treads with Salt Cure. Protect also stalls turns, which works well in conjunction with Salt Cure and allows Garganacl to chip its foes as much as possible; it's also useful at scouting moves from foes such as Choice Band Dragapult, Lokix, and Meowscarada and maximizing passive recovery from Leftovers. However, Ice Punch is a niche option to immediately nail Hydrapple and Gliscor, as they can be huge threats in the balance mirrors in general and shrug off Salt Cure's passive damage with Regenerator and Poison Heal. Additionally, the move also lets Garganacl chunk foes like Meowscarada, Dragapult, and Latios immediately. Heavy-Duty Boots is an option on teams with little to no hazard removal at the cost of crucial Leftovers recovery. 52 Defense EVs allow Garganacl to survive Ogerpon-W's Power Whip, and the rest of the EVs are invested in HP and Special Defense to maximize its special bulk to help it take on threats such as Dragapult in a better fashion. Tera Fairy enables it to handle threats such as Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Dragapult better; in addition, the Grass neutrality helps it against foes like Rillaboom, Ogerpon-W, and Meowscarada. Tera Water helps it against foes like Gholdengo and Water-types like Barraskewda and Hisuian Samurott. Both of these Tera types are useful at handling non-Swords Dance Gliscor as well, as Garganacl also acts as a Toxic absorber.

Garganacl fits well on bulky offense and balance teams that need a bulky entry hazard setter; Salt Cure is great at making progress for its teammates to capitalize on. Setup sweepers such as Kingambit, Weavile, and Nasty Plot Gholdengo appreciate Garganacl's ability to chip and force damage on the opposing team with Stealth Rock and Salt Cure, especially against threats such as Skarmory and Primarina. In return, they offensively pressure Garganacl's switch-ins such as Galarian Slowking, Rillaboom, and Clefable, as it's reliant on Salt Cure for damage and is thus very passive. Gholdengo also deserves a special mention because of its ability to block hazard removal attempts from foes like Great Tusk and Corviknight. Garganacl also forms amazing cores with Spikes setters such as Gliscor, Hisuian Samurott, and Skarmory, further helping its offensive teammates by dominating the hazard game. Moreover, Gliscor and Skarmory also help it in checking Ground- and Fighting-types like Landorus-T and Zamazenta. Knock Off users such as Clefable and the aforementioned Weavile are also good teammates due to removing Heavy-Duty Boots from foes such as Galarian Slowking and Dondozo; removing Leftovers from foes like Zamazenta and Ting-Lu is also useful so that they take maximum damage from Salt Cure and Stealth Rock. In addition, Clefable and the aforementioned Gliscor also support Garganacl by acting as Knock Off absorbers, as Garganacl likes to keep its Leftovers intact—Protect and Leftovers form a strong combination that makes Garganacl very tough to break down. Galarian Slowking also makes a great partner that supports Garganacl with Future Sight, punishing Fighting-types such as Zamazenta and Iron Valiant, as well as providing pivoting support with Chilly Reception. Garganacl also appreciates hazard removal support, as its foes such as Gliscor, Clefable, and Ting-Lu may use it as fodder for setting up hazards, especially Spikes; as such, Pokemon like Great Tusk make nice teammates. Due to its relatively poor base typing, Garganacl is weak to a variety of threats including Great Tusk, Iron Valiant, Kingambit, and Ogerpon-W; thus, partners such as Ogerpon-W, Skeledirge, Zamazenta, and Dragapult, respectively, are appreciated. Rillaboom also synergizes well with Garganacl, as its Grassy Terrain can weaken Earthquake from foes like Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, and Gliscor for Garganacl as well as helping it deal with Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Barraskewda; in return, Garganacl supports Rillaboom with hazard and deals with foes like Iron Moth for it.

movesets.name: Curse
movesets.description:
Garganacl's incredible defensive stats and access to Salt Cure make it a potent Curse user, letting it beat threatening physical attackers such as Weavile and Dragon Dance Dragonite while acting as a pseudo-sweeper. Earthquake lets Garganacl hit threats such as Gholdengo, Raging Bolt, and Galarian Slowking, with its high-Base Power giving Garganacl offensive presence so it doesn't have to rely solely on Salt Cure for damage, which is especially useful since Raging Bolt commonly runs Leftovers and Galarian Slowking's Regenerator can mitigate Salt Cure damage as well. 52 Defense EVs lets Garganacl survive Ogerpon-W's Power Whip without the need for Curse boosts or Terastallization. Tera Water turns Garganacl's Water weakness into a resistance, letting it better handle Water-types such as Barraskewda and Hisuian Samurott. It also lets Garganacl check offensive Steel-types such as Gholdengo, with Purifying Salt letting it resist Shadow Ball. On the other hand, Tera Fairy gives Garganacl an immunity to Draco Meteor from Dragapult as well as Dragon Pulse from Raging Bolt. It also grants Garganacl a resistance to Fighting-type moves from Pokemon such as Zamazenta and Great Tusk and removes its Grass weakness, improving its matchup against Meowscarada. Both options remove Garganacl's weakness to Ground-type moves, letting it better handle foes that rely on Earthquake for coverage such as Dragonite.

Garganacl fits well on bulky offense or balance teams. Due to not running Heavy-Duty Boots, Garganacl appreciates entry hazard removal from the likes of Great Tusk and Corviknight; Great Tusk in particular appreciates Garganacl checking spinblockers such as Dragapult and, with Tera Water, Gholdengo. Rillaboom makes for a great partner thanks to Garganacl appreciating the recovery from Grassy Terrain, which alleviates entry hazard chip damage, as well as the reduction in Earthquake's damage, letting it check Pokemon like Dragonite better. It should be noted that Garganacl's own Earthquake will deal less damage as a result of Grassy Terrain and Salt Cure's chip damage will be mitigated by Grassy Terrain's healing when combined with Leftovers, however. As Substitute blocks Salt Cure, Pokemon that can punish the use of the move, such as Encore Dragonite, Infiltrator Dragapult, and Whirlwind Ting-Lu, are appreciated teammates. Ogerpon-W makes for a great partner with Garganacl thanks to Water Absorb and its ability to force Ground-types like Gliscor out with Ivy Cudgel. It can also punish Substitute with Encore and remove items like Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off, accentuating the chip damage done by Salt Cure. In exchange, it appreciates Garganacl deterring defensive Pokemon like Skarmory with Salt Cure, as well as its ability to handle Dragon-types like Dragonite and Dragapult. Unaware Clefable forms a good defensive core with Garganacl, denying other setup sweepers the opportunity to set up on Garganacl while also appreciating its ability to absorb status from Pokemon like Galarian Slowking, Dragapult and Skeledirge. Garganacl also benefits from Clefable's ability to check Ting-Lu. Opposing Clefable can check Garganacl with both of its abilities, so Pokemon that can dispatch it, like Gholdengo and Heatran, make for good partners. Garganacl also enjoys Knock Off and hazard support, as the removal of items like Heavy-Duty Boots and the additional chip from hazards makes it harder to play around due to the chip damage from Salt Cure having more of an impact on Pokemon like Galarian Slowking, Alomomola, and Ting-Lu. Gliscor has access to Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Knock Off while also resisting Ground-type moves; in exchange, Garganacl checks Hex Dragapult, one of Gliscor's best checks. Finally, specially defensive Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking and Clodsire appreciate Garganacl's physical walling capabilities while making up for its inability to consistently handle special attackers like Primarina and Enamorus.

movesets.name: Iron Defense
movesets.description:
With fantastic bulk, Salt Cure, Purifying Salt's status immunity, the combination of Iron Defense and Body Press, and reliable recovery, Garganacl establishes itself as a potent win condition. Iron Defense lets Garganacl boost its Defense to nearly unbreakable levels. Body Press allows Garganacl to threaten the likes of Kingambit, Ting-Lu, and Weavile, and with Iron Defense boosts, Garganacl's Body Press becomes more threatening, 2HKOing the likes of Iron Treads and Kyurem after just one boost. In tandem with Salt Cure, Gliscor can eventually be beaten with enough Iron Defense boosts. Salt Cure pressures would-be switch-ins like Ogerpon-W, Gholdengo, and Dondozo. Leftovers adds even more to Garganacl's excellent survivability, allowing it to conserve valuable Recover PP, further complemented by Iron Defense boosts that enhance its ability to take physical attacks. Tera Water allows Garganacl to resist Steel- and Water-type moves that threaten it, such as Make It Rain, Tachyon Cutter, Razor Shell, and Ivy Cudgel from Gholdengo, Iron Crown, Hisuian Samurott, and Ogerpon-W, respectively. It also removes Garganacl's weakness to Ground-type moves, making it even harder for Great Tusk and Dragonite to break through it. Tera Electric grants a Steel resistance while lacking weaknesses, and the singular Ground weakness it has is offset by most Ground-type attacks being physical, which, with Iron Defense boosts, can be offset. However, Ground-type coverage from Enamorus and Kyurem still threatens Garganacl. Tera Fairy removes Garganacl's weakness to Fighting, though Pokemon that use Fighting-type attacks can hit it with other attacks, like Psycho Boost from Deoxys-S. Its main benefit comes from the fact that Fairy is a generally good defensive typing that doesn't give Garganacl many other weaknesses. It grants a Dark resistance, which is useful for Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott, and Dragon immunity, useful against Raging Bolt and Walking Wake.

Garganacl fits on balance and bulky offense teams that can support its Iron Defense sweeps and cover its vulnerability to entry hazards. Hazards set by Ting-Lu, Ogerpon-W, and Clefable complement Garganacl's Salt Cure pressure and the switches it forces with Iron Defense boosting. Ogerpon-W in particular can pressure Great Tusk, Gliscor, and Ting-Lu, allowing Garganacl to preserve HP for other physical threats, and can function as a pivot by virtue of forcing out these Ground-types and using U-turn to bring Garganacl in safely or as a wallbreaker that threatens Hatterene and Calm Mind Clefable, both of which Garganacl struggles against. In return, Garganacl can take on Dragapult and, if Garganacl Terastallizes, Dragonite, both of which can check Ogerpon-W. Great Tusk and Iron Treads synergize nicely with Garganacl, as their Rapid Spin does not clear away hazards set by other teammates such as Ogerpon-W and Clefable. In return, Garganacl checks Dragapult and Zapdos for Great Tusk and Fire-types such as Cinderace and Ceruledge for Iron Treads. Gholdengo checks many of Garganacl's difficult matchups, such as Clefable, Hatterene, Galarian Slowking, and Galarian Weezing, which all threaten or cripple Garganacl. Defoggers such as Corviknight and Galarian Weezing are great partners as well, as both can compress the roles of hazard remover and check to Rillaboom, Ogerpon-W, and Zamazenta, which greatly threaten this Garganacl set without any Defense boosts. While they don't remove hazards, Moltres, Tornadus-T, and Dragapult can all similarly function as checks to some of the aforementioned Pokemon as well as to other Grass-types such as Hydrapple and Sinistcha, while Garganacl checks Zapdos for the first two and Choice Scarf Enamorus for the latter. While this Garganacl set fully invests in Special Defense, special walls such as Galarian Slowking and Ting-Lu can cover for special attackers such as Raging Bolt, Iron Crown, and Gholdengo that would greatly weaken Garganacl otherwise.

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Tera Fairy allows Garganacl to wall Koraidon fully, but since it prevents Garganacl from walling Arceus and Substitute Ho-Oh, this set is not regularly used. Garganacl could also opt to use Curse, increasing the damage of Salt Cure while simultaneously allowing Garganacl to keep up with boosting threats. Yet, the additional Salt Cure damage is inconsequential, and it takes many more turns for Garganacl to do the same amount of damage with Body Press if it were instead using Iron Defense.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Special attackers like Kyogre, Miraidon, and Calyrex-S can easily exploit Garganacl's poor special defenses to threaten massive damage.

Koraidon: Koraidon's super effective Low Kick does great damage to Garganacl, forcing it to switch out even after an Iron Defense boost.

Knock Off Users: Knock Off users like Gliscor significantly cripple Garganacl's defensive capabilities, causing it to be much less effective in checking Pokemon like Earthquake Ho-Oh after some entry hazard chip damage.

Zacian-C: Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, especially in combination with Swords Dance, tears through even boosted Garganacl's HP and forces it to switch out.

Necrozma-DM: Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike, in combination with a move like Dragon Dance or Swords Dance, threatens great damage to Garganacl, forcing it to switch out.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
Salt Cure puts a timer on any Pokemon attempting to set up against Garganacl while also breaking offensive Ho-Oh's Substitute and dealing considerable damage to Zacian-C, Giratina-O, and Kyogre that try to switch in. Iron Defense allows Garganacl to keep up with Swords Dance Arceus and also allows it to check Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground after Terastallization. The IronPress combination allows Garganacl to do significant damage to Pokemon like Arceus and anything else that attempts to switch in. Alternatively, Stealth Rock further chips defensive Arceus formes and Choice Scarf users, allowing Garganacl to aid its team. Body Press, usually used in conjunction with Iron Defense, allows Garganacl to become a late-game sweeper while also dealing considerable damage to more offensive Pokemon like Arceus, Arceus-Ground, and Koraidon. Protect lets Garganacl safely scout Choice item users, like Choice Band Koraidon and Choice Specs Kyogre, as well as provide an additional turn of Salt Cure chip damage. Tera Flying gives Garganacl an immunity to Arceus-Ground, Landorus-T, and Ting-Lu's Earthquake, as well as a resistance to Koraidon's Low Kick and Calyrex-S's Grass Knot. On the other hand, Tera Water gives Garganacl a resistance to Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike, Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance, and Kyogre's Water-type attacks in a pinch. Garganacl is an especially effective Ho-Oh check, as Purifying Salt nullifies its Sacred Fire burns.

Physically frail Pokemon like Blissey and Clodsire enjoy having Garganacl on their team, as it excels in checking both Extreme Killer and Bulk Up Arceus. Even physically defensive Pokemon like Gliscor, various bulky Water-types, and Skeledirge appreciate Garganacl for its ability to wall both offensive Ho-Oh sets and Giratina-O with ease. However, although Garganacl can wall many physical threats, its special defenses are lacking. Powerful special attackers like Kyogre, Miraidon, and Calyrex-S can easily break through Garganacl. Thus, Garganacl appreciates having teammates like Blissey, Specially Defensive Ho-Oh, and Clodsire, which find it far easier to handle special-attacking threats. Although Garganacl has excellent defenses, it still cannot handle super effective hits from Koraidon, Zacian-C, Arceus-Ground, and Necrozma-DM. Pokemon like Alomomola, Skeledirge, and Gliscor, which switch into their attacks, are very effective when paired with Garganacl.

movesets.name: IronPress
movesets.description:
Garganacl eases the Water and Steel matchups thanks to its signature move, Salt Cure. Iron Defense allows Garganacl to set up, tanking super effective physical hits due to its astronomical base 130 Defense, while also boosting the power of Body Press, which helps nail Dark- and Steel-types such as Ting-Lu, Chien-Pao, and Kingambit. Curse is another option that can buff its Attack, boosting the damage of Salt Cure, but it prevents Garganacl from easily stonewalling physical attackers—such as Dragonite and defensive Quaquaval—and also lowers Garganacl's Speed. Salt Cure is a fantastic STAB move, neutering setup sweepers such as Mimikyu, Corviknight, and Hatterene, as it puts them on a timer, which Garganacl can potentially stall out as it sets up or heals via Recover. Purifying Salt is particularly useful, as it allows Garganacl to absorb incoming status moves such as Toxic from Quagsire or Toxapex as well as Will-O-Wisp from Dragapult or Sableye and punish them with Salt Cure. Garganacl is also able to tank Ghost-type STAB moves from the likes of Choice-locked Flutter Mane and Dragapult. Leftovers is the best item to provide passive recovery; however, Heavy-Duty Boots can allow Garganacl to come in without taking entry hazard damage, as entry hazard stacking is extremely common. As an alternative to the given EVs, 52 Defense EVs with an Impish nature let Garganacl potentially overwhelm Choice Band Scizor, Tinkaton, and defensive Quaquaval if used with Iron Defense.

Tyranitar is an amazing partner for Garganacl, as it sets sand. Tyranitar can also be used as one of the few special attackers Rock teams have access to to nail physical walls such as Great Tusk with Ice Beam; it is also Rock's best check to Kingambit due to it being able to survive a boosted Sucker Punch and OHKO back with Fire Blast. Choice Scarf Glimmora can take on Grass- and Fighting-types such as Breloom and Iron Valiant that may threaten Garganacl out. Glimmora also has fantastic coverage, being able to take on Steel-types such as Gholdengo with Earth Power and Water-types such as Gastrodon and Quagsire with Energy Ball. Glimmora can also provide Toxic Spikes support thanks to its ability, Toxic Debris, which can help Garganacl further wear down and pressure the opposing Pokemon. Teammates that utilize Air Balloon such as Iron Thorns and Drednaw can switch into powerful Ground-type attacks aimed at Garganacl. Drednaw can also utilize its Water-type STAB move to take out opposing Ground-types such as Iron Treads, Unaware Clodsire, and Ting-Lu. Furthermore, Drednaw can also turn the tide against rain Water teams thanks to its ability, Swift Swim. Lycanroc-D is also a really good partner for Garganacl that appreciates its ability to wear down foes so it can clean up late-game. Coalossal is also a good partner that can not only burn foes but also lay down entry hazards. Coalossal can also clear its side of the field as well with Rapid Spin, alleviating chip damage on the team. It also acts as a soft check to Scizor and Meowscarada due to its neutralities and can potentially neuter them with Flame Body.

movesets.name: Salty Stall
movesets.description:
• With some entry hazard support, this Garganacl can be very difficult to outstall, thanks to the constant passive damage from Salt Cure.

  • Protect: Not only does Protect scout for surprise Tera types, but it also goes well with the passive healing from Leftovers.

  • Stealth Rock: Since this set benefits so much from Stealth Rock support, running it on its own is a reasonable sacrifice if Garganacl needs to be more self-sufficient.

  • Substitute: This makes Garganacl even more difficult to properly switch into, providing protection against Trick, OHKO moves, and opposing Salt Cure.

  • Fissure: Garganacl's great bulk makes it a prime candidate for fishing with Fissure itself, though its low PP can be an issue in mirror matches.

Other Options

  • Fling with Light Ball, Toxic Orb, or Flame Orb: Although the loss of Leftovers can be a huge blow for Garganacl, Fling and its associated status inducing items can be a devastating surprise for some of its checks, such as Annihilape and Urshifu formes. Just note that Covert Cloak will still block these statuses.

  • Sturdy and Custap Berry: Getting rid of Garganacl's status immunity and Ghost resistance is a huge sacrifice, but it can let Garganacl lead against some surprising Pokemon effectively without needing to Terastallize, like Choice Specs Chi-Yu and Iron Bundle. Custap Berry's pseudo-priority can also lead to surprising Stealth Rock set-ups.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While Rock may be an awful defensive typing, this Garganacl's complete focus on taking advantage of Salt Cure means that in some scenarios, it can get away without Terastallizing.

  • Poison: Tera Poison's Fighting and Fairy-type resistance vastly improves Garganacl's match-up against Flutter Mane, Ogerpon-H, and Urshifu-R, making it a prime Tera choice. As a bonus, this also lets Garganacl absorb Toxic Spikes.

  • Water: Tera Water gives Garganacl a better matchup against Chien-Pao, Urshifu-R, and Gholdengo, in addition to being an excellent defensive typing.

  • Ghost: While removing Purifying Salt's Ghost resistance is a shame, Tera Ghost does wonderfully against Archaludon and opposing Garganacl due to the Body Press immunity, and in general removes all of Garganacl's common weaknesses. Tera Ghost also can make foes paranoid of it being the Curse set.

  • Flying: Tera Flying gets rid of the Ground and Fighting weaknesses, giving it a far better chance of beating Landorus-T and Ursaluna-B. It also makes Fissure no longer an issue from Ting-Lu, Dondozo, and opposing Garganacl.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy lets Garganacl tank powerful Fighting coverage such as Chien-Pao's Scared Sword, and shrug off powerful Dragon-type attacks from Latios and Roaring Moon.

movesets.name: Curse
movesets.description:
• With Curse's well-known different effect for Ghost-types being brought into play by Terastallization, Garganacl makes dangerous and diverse use of the move! Boosting Salt Cure's meager power can also help against frailer Substitute users such as Flutter Mane.

  • Tera Ghost Curse: If using Tera Ghost, Curse will change its effect, which drastically changes Garganacl's playstyle. While the 50% health cut can make it a tad risky, the Curse affliction is very powerful at wearing down Pokemon, including major foes that take advantage of Salt Cure, such as Covert Cloak Pokemon, bulky Substitute users, and Blaziken Baton Pass chains. When combined with Salt Cure, it can even overwhelm bulky Pokemon with recovery, such as Dragonite.

  • Curse and Earthquake: Ghost Curse unfortunately does not work against Gholdengo, so using regular Curse alongside Earthquake makes Garganacl far less passive against against Gholdengo and frail Substitute users such as Flutter Mane. This is especially recommended if using other Tera types.

  • Protect versus Substitute: Protect is perfect for getting some extra Leftovers recovery, but Substitute comes in handy against Dragon Tail users like Archaludon and Garchomp.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Salt Cure means Garganacl can still without Terastallization, but to truly take advantage of either facet of Curse, expect to Terastallize it often.

  • Ghost: In addition to being a great defensive typing that leaves Garganacl with only a weakness to Dark thanks to Purifying Salt, this is the Tera type that enables the unique properties of Curse.

  • Poison: Tera Poison is Garganacl's best option against Flutter Mane, ensuring it resists both STAB attacks. Absorbing Toxic Spikes is also helpful against stall teams.

  • Water: If messing with Gholdengo is the goal, Tera Water is an excellent choice, resisting the powerful Make It Rain and being a good defensive typing in general.

  • Fairy: Beyond being a great typing that offers a Fighting-type resistance, it also means Garganacl no longer has to worry about Dragon Tail from Archaludon. This doesn't improve Garganacl's match-up against Gholdengo though.

  • Flying: Tera Flying has excellent synergy with Garganacl's former typing, making it immune to Landorus-T and Ursaluna-B's Ground-type attacks, and even removing any worry about Fissure from Ting-Lu and Dondozo. However, this comes at the cost of still making it vulnerable to Iron Bundle.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
• With Purifying Salt making it immune to status and Salt Cure providing useful chip damage, especially against Water- and Steel-types, Garganacl is a dangerous defensive setup Pokemon.

  • Iron Defense and Body Press: Body Press is the best option for consistency against offensive teams.

  • Fissure: Fissure severely punishes passive play against Garganacl, at the cost of forcing it to rely on Salt Cure residual damage against offensive teams.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Rock has a huge amount of weaknesses as a defensive typing, so Garganacl will usually want to Terastallize to make sweeping more feasible.

  • Poison: Tera Poison is the prime pick to combat Flutter Mane, with it making Garganacl resist both Moonblast and Shadow Ball. The Fighting-type resistance against Urshifu formes and Toxic Spikes absorption is also quite helpful.

  • Water: Tera Water vastly improves Garganacl's chances of defeating Gholdengo, Urshifu-R, and Chien-Pao.

  • Ghost: A Ghost Tera type gives Garganacl an immunity to Body Press, giving it the edge against Archaludon and opposing Garganacl, especially when paired with Leftovers. It can also fool players into thinking Garganacl is using the Curse set.

  • Flying: A Flying typing lets Garganacl take on new foes such as Landorus-T, Ursaluna-B, and Garchomp, though it makes Garganacl fairly weak to Iron Bundle and Chien-Pao

  • Fairy: Fairy is a good defensive type for Garganacl, giving it a useful Fighting and Dark resistance to help against Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu, and no longer worrying about powerful Dragon-type attacks. However, Garganacl still remains vulnerable to powerful Steel-type attacks from foes like Gholdengo. EV Spreads ========

  • 252 HP / 252 SpD / 4 Spe with Careful: Maximizing Special Defense is the best choice for easier setup.

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spe with Impish: In addition to powering up Body Press, a focus on Defense makes setting up on powerful setup sweepers such as Dragonite an easier task.

  • 252 HP / 84 Def / 172 SpD with Careful: This EV spread allows Tera Steel Garganacl to avoid a 2HKO from Breloom's Mach Punch after Iron Defense.

movesets.name: The Salt Cure
movesets.description: Garganacl is a tough defensive wall that uses Salt Cure to wear down defensive Pokemon, like Swampert, Great Tusk, and Corviknight, and utilizes its ability selection to check a variety of different Pokemon. Fluffy allows Garganacl to check Kingambit and Iron Boulder, Water Absorb lets it reliably switch in on defensive Manaphy as well as help with checking Choice-locked Water-types like Barraskewda and Primarina, and Earth Eater lets it check Roaring Moon and Dragonite running Earthquake. Stealth Rock lets Garganacl support its teammates by providing entry hazards, while with Iron Defense or Curse, Garganacl can set up on and more easily check Pokemon like Iron Hands, Ceruledge, and Dragonite, and boost Body Press or Earthquake, depending on the set. When using Body Press, Garganacl can more efficiently take on Chien-Pao as well as a majority of other Pokemon, while with Earthquake, it can deal with Iron Boulder and Pecharunt. Protect lets Garganacl deal extra damage with Salt Cure active as well as gain some extra Leftovers recovery. Garganacl can either use Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots, the former letting it gain more recovery through Protect and the latter helping Garganacl switch in more often. Garganacl provides great defensive support to frail offensive Pokemon, like Iron Moth, Gengar, and Galarian Zapdos, as a to check faster Pokemon like Roaring Moon, Dragonite, and Iron Boulder. Garganacl can struggle against special attackers, such as Deoxys-S, Azelf, and offensive Gholdengo, so having specially defensive teammates, like Hisuian Goodra, Manaphy, and Blissey, can help. Garganacl enjoys being on more defensive teams for having teammates that can take on physical attackers with it, such as Pecharunt, Mandibuzz, and Primarina, as it struggles to reliably check Pokemon like Chien-Pao, Zamazenta, and Barraskewda.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 5 onwards

Price Range: 6-7 points

Overview: Garganacl is a solid defensive Pokemon that can force opponents to make difficult decisions in the teambuilder. Its defensive stats alongside Purifying Salt means it is difficult for foes to break through without damage-boosting items or moves, and playing the long game to wear it down is difficult because of Salt Cure and Recover. Garganacl can also be a setup sweeper, since its defensive stats and Recover alongside Curse or Iron Defense and Body Press means teams can have difficulty getting it off the field. However, its awful defensive typing and the ability to negate all of the passive damage of Salt Cure with a single item means that in many games, its impact is much lower than expected.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Wall: Using its great defensive stats and reliable recovery, Garganacl is a great wall that can dish out damage with Salt Cure and set Stealth Rock while staying healthy with Recover.

Setup Sweeper: Whether using IronPress or Curse, Garganacl can quickly become a problem for teams not prepared for Salt Cure's residual damage alongside its longevity and boosted moves.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Salt Cure, Rock Slide, Stone Edge

Setup Moves: Curse, Iron Defense

Utility Moves: Stealth Rock, Recover, Substitute, Protect

Coverage: Earthquake, Body Press, Ice Punch, Fire Punch, Avalanche, Hammer Arm, Heavy Slam, Zen Headbutt, Thunder Punch

Niche Moves

Bulldoze / Rock Tomb: While Bulldoze and Rock Tomb deal less damage than Garganacl's other coverage options, lowering a foe's Speed can be very useful for teammates.

Block: Against passive foes, Block can allow Garganacl to deal with the target or set up freely without needing to worry about it switching to a more threatening Pokemon.

Endure: Endure can be used to ensure the activation of items like Red Card and Custap Berry.

Explosions: Explosion is a useful option to maintain momentum on sets that are more focused around setting entry hazards for teammates than its defensive duties.

Common Items

Leftovers: Since Garganacl is usually on the field for many turns consecutively, Leftovers allows it to get a little extra out of each turn, helping it wall foes and drag out games for Salt Cure damage.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Avoiding entry hazard damage can mean the difference between Garganacl being able to switch into an attack or not, making them a solid Leftovers alternative.

Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet is a solid choice for punishing physical attackers and foes using contact moves.

Niche Items

Custap Berry: Custap Berry is a solid pick on sets utilizing Endure to get off a last minute Salt Cure or Explosion that foes may not expect.

Red Card: Thanks to its solid defensive profile, Garganacl can take most non-super effective attacks and trigger Red Card to force the foe out. Endure is also an option to guarantee a foe is forced out.

Resistance Berries: Generally, Garganacl should not be taking super effective hits, but if necessary, resistance Berries can allow it to get off a crucial Salt Cure when a foe thinks they can KO it.

Mental Herb: Since Garganacl is prone to disruption, Mental Herb can help it avoid letting foes get free setup turns in the case of Encore or losing access to recovery in the case of Taunt.

Eject Button: Garganacl can be a real momentum hog, so Eject Button allows it to switch in and then get out without risking a teammate taking damage.

Tera

For a low-tier Pokemon, Garganacl is a Tera hog. It often benefits from ditching its awful Rock typing for a better defensive type like Tera Fairy, Water, and Steel; however, this means planning to Tera an cheap Pokemon many games and not Terastallizing a higher-tier Pokemon. When using Terastallization, Garganacl becomes an ever stronger wall and more threatening setup sweeper that can take advantage of foes it normally would not be able to check. Tera Fighting is a solid option on IronPress sets if aiming to sweep, while Tera Ghost leaves it weak to only one type; however, Curse sets cannot use Tera Ghost, so plan carefully.

Draft Strategy

Garganacl's ability to be either physically or specially defensive, but not outstanding at either, means it pairs well with teammates that can cover the defense it is not investing in. It also makes a great partner for entry hazard-focused drafts, since opponents are forced to choose between using Heavy-Duty Boots or Covert Cloak on their Pokemon.

Defensive Pivots: Pokemon like Slowking, Corviknight, and Mandibuzz that can scout the sets foes are running and bring Garganacl into the right matchups help it survive throughout a game and maximize its impact while also taking defensive pressure off of it.

Entry Hazard Setters: Since Garganacl can force foes into using a sub-optimal item like Covert Cloak, having strong entry hazard support from Pokemon like Ting-Lu, Hisuian Samurott, and Glimmora can punish them for not running Heavy-Duty Boots.

Knock Off Users: Since Garganacl's best move is negated by Covert Cloak, Knock Off users like Meowscarada, Weavile, and Roaring Moon can help ensure foes are taking every bit of Salt Cure damage possible.

Sweepers: Between forcing an awkward item and passive damage from Salt Cure, Garganacl can wear down an opponent's team for sweepers like Greninja and Sneasler to come in and clean up.

Checks and Counters

Covert Cloak / Magic Guard: Covert Cloak negates all Salt Cure damage and makes it extremely difficult for Garganacl to make progress, as it relies on Salt Cure to keep up damage on foes while it is recovering or trying to set up its own boosts. Magic Guard also fills a similar role by denying the passive damage of Salt Cure.

Substitute: Much like Covert Cloak, Substitute prevents Salt Cure's secondary effect from being applied, allowing foes to be completely safe to set up in front of many Garganacl sets.

Wallbreakers: Garganacl's defensive stats are solid, but Pokemon like Ogerpon, Enamorus, and both Urshifu formes can still break through it.

Disruption: Moves like Encore and Taunt can cripple Garganacl, as it needs access to its full moveset to function well and relies on many status moves such as Recover.

movesets.name: Setup
movesets.description: Garganacl acts as an anti-metagame setup sweeper with the potential to clean up games with enough boosts and Salt Cure to punish Steel- and Water-types like Magearna, Solgaleo, and Palkia-O that might try to switch in to deal with it. Garganacl can use Iron Defense to become unbeatable on the physical side, while its stats give it enough bulk to survive most special attacks comfortably. Alternatively, it can use Curse to boost its attack and hit harder with Salt Cure or a coverage move, although this is considerably slower than Iron Defense. Body Press is used to take advantage of Iron Defense's boosts while also hitting Arceus-Dark and Chi-Yu for supereffective, while Earthquake provides better coverage against Pokemon like Giratina and Slowking-Galar if Garganacl is using Curse as its boosting move. Leftovers gives Garganacl some passive healing, allowing it to heal while setting up, although Heavy-Duty Boots can be used instead. Tera Water allows Garganacl to resist Water-type attacks from Pokemon like Palkia-O and Palafin, while Tera Fairy can be used to give it an immunity to Dragon-type attacks, more specifically preventing Dragon Tail from Dialga and Giratina from phazing it. Physical attackers that struggle against Giratina like Zamazenta-C and Palafin appreciate Garganacl's ability to absorb status and resist Ghost. Teammates that struggle against Chi-Yu or Magearna, such as Chien-Pao and Mewtwo, greatly benefit from Garganacl's ability to check these foes. Garganacl struggles against Grass- and Water-type Pokemon like Rillaboom and Palkia-O, so teammates that can switch into their attacks like Arceus-Grass and Dialga form a very solid defensive core with it

movesets.name: Stealth Rock
movesets.description: Garganacl is a great defensive tool within Ubers UU, being able to comfortably set Stealth Rock against both of the tier's best entry hazard removal options in Giratina and Terapagos. Protect synergizes well with Salt Cure and allows Garganacl to scout moves from Choice-locked Chien-Pao, Landorus, Palafin, and Palkia. Tera Water provides Garganacl with a resistance to Steel- and Water-type moves such as Make It Rain from Gholdengo and Hydro Pump from both Palkia formes and retains its Fire resistance so it can handle Chi-Yu. Tera Fairy allows Garganacl to cover its weakness to Fighting-type moves such as Focus Blast from Landorus and Mewtwo and provides an immunity to Dragon-type moves such as Palkia-O's Spacial Rend, Kyurem-W's Draco Meteor, and Giratina's Dragon Tail. Garganacl can use Heavy-Duty Boots as an alternative to Leftovers on teams lacking hazard removal or to improve the matchup into Spikes Magearna. Garganacl fits best on stall and fat balance teams using Giratina and Toxapex for excellent hazard control and passive damage support. Garganacl loses to two important Ghost-types, Spectrier and Necrozma-DW, due to their combination of setup moves and recovery. Fast physical attackers such as Zacian and Chien-Pao can scare out both Pokemon, and tanky Dark-types such as Arceus-Dark can be used to answer Necrozma-DW regardless of its set.

movesets.name: SpDef Wall (SpD, HP)
movesets.description:
Garganacl is a premier wall that leverages its incredible bulk, unique ability, and decent utility to consistently wear down opponents over time. Salt Cure is the cornerstone of the set, providing chip damage every turn. When combined with Protect, Garganacl can safely stall turns to rack up Salt Cure damage and Leftovers recovery, making it extremely difficult to outlast. Recover gives Garganacl the reliable healing it needs to continually check powerful special attackers like Iron Moth and Darkrai across a long battle. Stealth Rock is generally preferred on Garganacl, but if the team already has the move covered, it can also run Curse, acting as a late-game wincon that becomes extremely bulky on both ends. When running Curse, Garganacl should also use Earthquake, which prevents it from becoming overly passive and allows it to hit targets like Necrozma-DM, Eternatus, and Galarian Slowking. Tera Water is the most consistent choice for Garganacl, removing its Steel and Water weaknesses while being an all-around good defensive typing. Alternatively, Tera Fairy flips its Fighting weakness, while Tera Ghost lets Garganacl spinblock Great Tusk while maintaining synergy with Purifying Salt.

Garganacl fits comfortably on balance and stall teams that appreciate its ability to spread passive damage and blanket check special attackers such as Iron Moth, Eternatus, and Darkrai. It thrives with high Special Defense donations from gods such as Calyrex-I and Ho-Oh, amplifying its already exceptional resilience and letting it wall powerful neutral hits with ease. However, HP donations from gods like Eternatus and Arceus are also acceptable. Since Garganacl thrives on chip damage, it appreciates Spikes setters like Hisuian Samurott, Ting-Lu, and Ogerpon, as well as spinblockers such as Pecharunt and Sinistcha to keep entry hazards up. Knock Off support is invaluable for Garganacl, since removing Heavy-Duty Boots, Leftovers, and Covert Cloak is very important for racking up chip damage. Thus, teammates like Iron Treads, Darkrai, and Weavile that can remove key items are highly appreciated.

movesets.name: Specially Defensive
movesets.description: Garganacl stands out as one of the tier's premier special walls, boasting exceptional bulk that grants it the ability to check special attackers such as Raging Bolt and Eternatus. With Sablenite, Garganacl's defenses are elevated even further while also granting it Magic Bounce, punishing attempts to set entry hazards except against Mold Breaker foes and allowing it to exploit common Pokemon such as Latiasite Magearna. Alternatively, Tyranitarite provides Garganacl with the Sand Stream ability, so it can increase its Special Defense even further and inflict additional chip damage through sand, which synergizes effectively with Salt Cure and hazards. Earthquake hits foes like Raging Bolt and non-Latiasite Magearna and Pecharunt, granting it somewhat of an offensive presence. Curse enhances Garganacl's ability to check physical attackers and can also be utilized to sweep opposing teams all while making it incredibly difficult to KO. Garganacl can even fulfill the role of a Stealth Rock setter by leveraging its ability to force switches and accumulate chip damage through Salt Cure. Garganacl thrives on balance teams and provides them with outstanding defensive utility; thus, pairing it with other bulky partners such as Magearna, Pecharunt, Arceus-Ground, and Ho-Oh creates a formidable core. Magearna has noteworthy synergy, as it also sets Spikes and capitalizes on Garganacl's ability to force switches through Salt Cure. Pokemon such as Arceus-Water, Urshifu-R, and Pinsirite Great Tusk as well as Latiasite users like Pecharunt and Magearna help Garganacl against troublesome Ground-type foes such as Arceus-Ground and Great Tusk. Offensive partners like Regieleki and Dragonite also form effective pairings with Garganacl, as they appreciate its capacity to wall threats like Eternatus, while in return, they can check foes such as Urshifu-R and Iron Boulder.

movesets.name: Iron Defense
movesets.description:
Garganacl's great bulk and exceptional ability in Purifying Salt make Garganacl a threatening, status-immune bulky setup sweeper that is able to check threatening Pokemon such as Iron Moth, Victini, and Blacephalon. Iron Defense makes Garganacl very difficult to overcome, even with super effective physical moves, while also boosting the power of Body Press, its main tool when sweeping. Salt Cure allows Garganacl to wear down potential checks, such as Rotom-W, Serperior, and Iron Crown; generate progress for its team; and punish Pokemon attempting to boost alongside it, namely Aegislash, Scizor, and Mega Latias. Curse is an alternative over Iron Defense to also boost Salt Cure's power at the cost of a lower gain in Defense; it also allows Garganacl to beat Pokemon such as Clefable and Enamorus that would otherwise check it by using Heavy Slam. Notably, Heavy Slam allows it to beat Magic Guard Clefable which is otherwise able to boost up alongside it thanks to being immune to Salt Cure's secondary effect.

This Garganacl set is best suited to balance teams, which appreciate it checking Pokemon such as Iron Moth and special variants of Aegislash while acting as a capable wincon that can make progress for its team. Since it beats most physical attackers after a boost or two, Garganacl highly values teammates that can handle the powerful special attackers that threaten it, namely Hydrapple, Keldeo, and Serperior, so Pokemon like Celesteela, Mega Latias, and Slowking make for valuable partners. Despite its impressive bulk, Garganacl's lack of useful resistances, low Speed, and large number of weaknesses to common attacking types mean it often struggles to come in safely, so slow pivots such as Scizor, Slowking, and Pecharunt are important allies to get it in. Pecharunt, in particular, can spread Toxic poison via Malignant Chain, amplifying the progress Salt Cure generates; Pecharunt also creates more setup opportunities via Parting Shot. Powerful physical attackers with super effective STAB moves such as Buzzwole, Rillaboom, and Life Orb Mienshao can threaten Garganacl even at +2, so Garganacl appreciates partners that can deal with these threats, such as Mega Venusaur, Skarmory, and Clefable. Knock Off can eliminate Garganacl's passive recovery, so Knock Off absorbers such as Clefable, Mega Pokemon like Mega Venusaur and Mega Aerodactyl, as well as Z-Move users like Hydrapple and Keldeo, are good choices to partner with Garganacl. Knock Off users on Garganacl's side, however, can remove Leftovers from opposing Pokemon like Hippowdon and Serperior that might otherwise limit Garganacl wearing the opposing team down with Salt Cure. Rillaboom's Grassy Terrain can create additional setup opportunities against Mega Aerodactyl and Toxic Hippowdon while giving some passive healing, letting Garganacl remain slightly healthier during the sweep, while Rillaboom itself can remove items with Knock Off and offer additional pivoting support via U-turn. When running Body Press, Pokemon that can threaten Clefable, such as Excadrill, Celesteela, and Iron Moth, are crucial, as Clefable is Garganacl's biggest roadblock.

movesets.name: Defensive Stealth Rock
movesets.description:
Garganacl can opt to be an effective Stealth Rock setter, using Salt Cure to punish common entry hazard control options like Rotom-W and Excadrill that would otherwise switch into it, as well as generate decent progress for its team. Protect is run in order to stall for additional rounds of Salt Cure damage and gain additional Leftovers recovery, additionally letting Garganacl scout out threatening moves like Tyranitar's Superpower and Iron Moth's Energy Ball. The 32 Defense EVs allow it to avoid being OHKOed by Choice Band Tyranitar's Superpower.

This set is best suited to balance teams looking for a reliable Stealth Rock user that checks special-attacking Aegislash sets and Iron Moth. As it is mostly reliant on Salt Cure's secondary effect to do damage, Garganacl is commonly exploited by Pokemon that either ignore or don't mind the chip damage such as Magic Guard Clefable and Regenerator users like Hydrapple and Mienshao. Therefore, Pokemon that check or exploit these threats such as Celesteela, Iron Crown, and Iron Moth are valued support. Garganacl struggles to switch in directly to many Pokemon due to its plethora of weaknesses to common types, so pivots such as Scizor, Pecharunt, and Slowking are greatly appreciated. Meanwhile, Garganacl can wear down the other team either via entry hazards or Salt Cure, giving these pivots an easier time forcing a switch to gain momentum for other teammates. Knock Off absorbers such as Z-Move users and Clefable are good picks, ensuring that Garganacl can retain its passive recovery while using Protect. Conversely, Knock Off users such as Clefable, Rillaboom, and Mienshao can support it by removing Leftovers from opposing Pokemon, which might otherwise dampen the passive damage of Salt Cure and prevent it from wearing down the opposing team to assist wallbreakers such as Mienshao, Hydrapple, and Buzzwole. Rillaboom in particular supports Garganacl with its Grassy Terrain, increasing its passive recovery even further and weakening Earthquakes that may otherwise threaten Garganacl while being able to get Garganacl in via U-turn.

movesets.name: Iron Defense
movesets.description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

movesets.name: IronPress
movesets.description:
• Garganacl's longevity allows it to act as a stallbreaker and a win condition against bulky teams thanks to the threat of Salt Cure. However, as it often heavily relies on Terastallizing to fix its vulnerability to Ground-types, combined with being easy to force out by special attackers, Garganacl is a niche pick for dedicated balance teams.
  • The IronPress combination ensures that Garganacl can check several physical foes such as defensive Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Extreme Killer Arceus without having to Terastallize, notably preventing itself from becoming setup fodder if an opponent such as Zygarde uses Substitute.
  • The given EV spread avoids a 2HKO from Basculegion-M's 300-Base Power Last Respects after Leftovers recovery, Dragon Dance Zygarde's Thousand Arrows, and special utility Giratina-O's Draco Meteor. This amount of bulk also avoids a 2HKO from Double Dance Primal Groudon's Precipice Blades after Garganacl has Terastallized.
  • Tera Water allows Garganacl to more comfortably come into Steel- and Water-types vulnerable to Salt Cure such as Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and Arceus-Water. Tera Fairy makes Garganacl hard wall Marshadow, support Arceus-Dark, and Giratina-O, and grants an immunity to Dragon Tail from foes such as Giratina-O and Zygarde, letting Garganacl preserve Iron Defense boosts.
  • Garganacl's main priority is to spread Salt Cure, wearing down the opposing team and granting its allies momentum as the opposing team is put into uncomfortable positions. Mid-game, Garganacl can be used as a check to physical attackers, as its status-absorbing capabilities also let it easily come into foes such as Ho-Oh, Alomomola, and Giratina-O. Late-game, it may try to apply offensive pressure with IronPress to threaten a sweep, as special attackers that can threaten Garganacl such as Yveltal and Eternatus are more vulnerable to Garganacl after getting worn down.
  • Against offensive team structures, Garganacl can find use against foes it can wall such as Extreme Killer Arceus and Rayquaza thanks to the IronPress combination, preventing it from being as easy to overwhelm on the physical side as it forces a switch, but if the momentum is disfavorable for it, Garganacl can still be used to hinder setup sweepers such as Necrozma-DM, Primal Kyogre, and Zacian-C, putting them on a timer and preventing them from doing much else without sacrificing momentum.
  • Garganacl has a positive matchup against the most common entry hazard removers in the metagame, notably including Ho-Oh and Giratina-O, so its presence can actively discourage them from entering the field, meaning that entry hazard setters such as Eternatus, Primal Groudon, and Ferrothorn make formidable allies.
  • Garganacl is generally vulnerable to special attackers such as Yveltal, Arceus-Fairy, and Primal Kyogre, so checks to them such as defensive Eternatus and Ferrothorn are notable options to mitigate this issue. Zacian-C is also a notable partner that can put offensive pressure on Garganacl's checks such as the previously mentioned foes.
  • Unless it has already Terastallized, Garganacl is vulnerable to Ground- and Fighting-type foes such as Primal Groudon, Arceus-Ground, and Marshadow. Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and Yveltal act as switch-ins to them for Garganacl to rely on early-game, with Garganacl in return limiting the longevity of their checks such as Chien-Pao and Extreme Killer Arceus.

movesets.name: Stealth Rock
movesets.description:
• Garganacl is an excellent option for bulkier balance teams in search of a resilient hazard setter. It is one of the best punishers of Defog in the tier and consequently is excellent at winning the hazard war. Garcanacl's excellent bulk, use of Tera, and ability to force progress via Salt Cure makes it a sturdy part of defensive cores. Unfortunately, Garganacl's reliance on Terastallizing requires specific support and hinders its splashability. As such, Garganacl works best when built with it in mind rather than slapping it on a team, especially given that its Tera type plays a huge role in what it is able to check.
  • Salt Cure has scarce switch-ins and prevents Garganacl from being passive while also punishing Defog attempts from Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and Choice Scarf Yveltal, none of which meaningfully hurt Garganacl.
  • Protect allows Garganacl to scout Choice-locked Pokemon such as Marshadow, Rayquaza, and Lunala. Additionally, it provides Garganacl with some minor healing and can accrue Salt Cure chip.
  • The given EV spread allows Garganacl to survive Life Orb Deoxys-A's Psycho Boost after Stealth Rock and avoid the 2HKO from Choice Band Tera Flying Rayquaza's Dragon Ascent. Additionally, it enables Garganacl to survive +1 Zacian-C's Close Combat and defensive Primal Groudon's Precipice Blades. 18 Speed IVs enable Garganacl to outspeed Calyrex-I under Trick Room.
  • Tera Water enables Garganacl to wall defensive Primal Kyogre. Tera Water Garganacl shrugs off any attack from it, and Salt Cure chip prevents Primal Kyogre from accumulating the boosts it needs to threaten Garganacl. Because Tera Water Garganacl also survives wallbreaker Primal Kyogre's Thunder after Stealth Rock, it can use Salt Cure to leave Primal Kyogre easily revenge killed or otherwise force it out. Additionally, Tera Water enables Garganacl to safely stall out defensive Primal Groudon and Zacian-C with Protect and Salt Cure in a pinch.
  • Tera Fairy Garganacl completely shuts down every Defogger. Although Garganacl isn't bothered by Giratina-O's Draco Meteor, preserving Recover PP is great for longer games. Tera Fairy also provides Garganacl with the unique trait of resisting Marshadow's STAB combination, which is highly valued by bulky teams worried about Choice Band Marshadow. Tera Fairy Garganacl can still survive an attack from wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, but has a harder time with defensive Primal Kyogre as it is 2HKOed by +1 Scald.
  • Garganacl has a presence in every stage of most games. Early-game, it will often set Stealth Rock while punishing switch-ins with Salt Cure. Garganacl is content to repeat the process mid-game, and it can act as a win condition end-game using Protect and Recover to allow Salt Cure chip to accumulate.
  • Garganacl partners well with Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and Eternatus to create a hazard stacking core where Salt Cure can prevent Pokemon such as Alomomola and Taunt Arceus formes, which can usually hinder hazard setters playing a similar role, from taking advantage of Garganacl. Forgoing a Defogger and relying on the pressure from entry hazards to pressure opponents to Defog is valid, but Ho-Oh nevertheless makes a good partner thanks to its consistency and defensive prowess, while Choice Scarf Yveltal partners well due to its ability to position with U-turn, revenge kill Pokemon such as Marshadow and Zacian-C, and consistently Defog at least once per game.
  • Garganacl often appreciates a teammate that can apply a direct source of offensive pressure to act as a win condition such as a Calm Mind Arceus forme or Zygarde. Although these Pokemon are self sufficient, their offensive presence is accentuated by Salt Cure chip. They appreciate Garganacl helping against Pokemon such as Ho-Oh and Primal Kyogre while Garganacl appreciates the help against Primal Groudon and Eternatus. Ditto also fills this role due to its ability to revenge kill most Pokemon on hyper offense teams that threaten to overwhelm Garganacl. Additionally, most Pokemon appreciate Garganacl's ability to act as a status sponge against defensive threats such as Ho-Oh and Eternatus.
